main_text.p: dere examinatur.Itaque cùm duo virtutis ex-trema vitiosa essent, rectè Horatius scripsisse creditur, Virtus est medium vitiorum vtrin-què redactum. Horum autem extremorum al-terum virtuti contrarium est, eáque pugnan-tia per se elucet: alterum difpar : quæ difpari-tas obscura est, quia virtutem fallaciter imi-tans eam adulterat.

Cedo exemplum. Plutarchus in Camillo hæc inter se opponit, δεισιδαιμονίαν & ὀλιγωρίαν τῷ θεῶν. ἡ δὲ εὐλαβεία (inquit) καὶ τὸ μηδὲν ἄγαν, ἀεισον[?]. Sic auaritia & prodigalitas vitia funt aduerfiffima. Interponatur liberalitas, contraria erit auaritiæ : difpar prodigalitati. Rurfus interponatur frugalitas,fiue parfimonia : contraria erit prodigalitati, difpar auaritiæ. Sic audacia & metus, duo vitia contraria funt. his interiecta fortitudo est, quæ metui contraria est,audaciæ difpar. Rurfus interponatur cautio:audaciæ cōtraria est, metui difpar.Ex eodem genere illa funt,quæ ex Ciceronis Partitionibus proferemus: Nā & prudentiam(inquit)malitia,& temperantiam immanitas in voluptatibus aspernandis, & magnitudinem animi superbia in animis extollendis, & defpicientia in contemnendis honoribus,&liberalitatem effufio,& fortitudinē audacia imitatur.& patiētiam duritia immanis, & iustitiam acerbitas, & religionem superstitio,& lenitaté mollitia animi, & verecundiam timiditas, & illam difputandi prudentiā con-

page.notes: Greek in the first paragraph is copied from a small, partly worn scan; "ὀλιγωρίαν" and the phrase after "τὸ μηδὲν ἄγαν" are doubtful and marked [?]. The printed "cùm", "quę", "rectè", "funt", "aduerfiffima", "fiue" and "cōtraria" are kept as printed. The printed "superbia" and "superstitio" keep the long s as a plain s. The right edge is a dark strip from the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. The two faint marks at the bottom left are not legible and are not transcribed. A small asterisk-like sign stands at the left of the last line, beside "certatio"; it is not transcribed.
